items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: We thought it was successful. Louis Armstrong.

ctx.x: But ironically enough, at the Tropicana we worked in the lounge, and the kind of crowd that was coming in, the interest that built up, meant that Maynard Sloat was bringing in things into the Blue Room, which was a room inside of the Tropicana too, the Blue Room. He brought in Count Basie, and he brought in Sarah Vaughan and Joe Williams. Then he brought in some of the Dixieland things, like Pete Fountain and Al Hirt, and there was Anita O'Day. And he brought in a few things into the Blue Room.

We thought it was successful. Louis Armstrong. We thought it was successful but obviously it didn't make it financially because it...those things in the big lounge. But at least there was some involvement with it. And I think it was...if someone in that...if a guy just got ahold of it and
stuck with it and made it happen, it would be no problem.
